items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: they would have a summer band with the parents and I would play trombone and my son would be playing the percussion

ctx.x: Yes. Believe it or not it was a weird kind of situation with my son. His mother passed two years ago and my former wife, I never married, we got a divorce kind of early in my son’s life but I never re-married. But he was always into music. Okay I’ll give you an example about him. At two years old he could play the piano and he would go [scats] “Popcorn” he had a song. He wrote all these songs. “Peanuts” and everything [scats] “Popcorn” [scats] so he was composing way back then, and then when I was playing the…

the summer I had the honor of, this was a friend of Ed Pasant. He’s not with us anymore. His daughter played the clarinet and Ed played the clarinet, and they would have a summer band with the parents and I would play trombone and my son would be playing the percussion and everything, and that was really, really nice. So my son, he never had like a day job, you know like kids wanted to work, you know at 7-Eleven or all these different stores, my son was the only child, so he got a job at 7-Eleven, and he was…
Yes and we’ve had the pleasure of his talents here at Hamilton College a number of times.
